title: GET {db}/vocabulary — the exposed types and edges
description: A name is only half of an agreement: a globally unique type name says nothing about whether the reader knows the shape behind it. This states each exposed type's fields so a caller can compare them with its own declaration and decline a type it cannot read through.

catalog.description: The responder's catalog version. Not a compatibility token.

projection.description: The named selection this database exposes, when it exposes one rather than its whole catalog.

fields.description: Empty for a type exposed only as an endpoint: an id a caller can hold and link to, with nothing to read.

counted.description: False for a field relationship, which follows an id in a payload and stores nothing — so it can be traversed but has no maintained counter to read.

foreign.description: Whether a target may be in another database. Optional, and absent means no: a vocabulary written before this member existed is still a conforming one. Where it is present, a caller can tell before it spends a request that the hop may leave this database — another round trip, and another database's policy behind it.
